newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bolivia and Mercosur finalize free-trade accord.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia and Mercosur finalize free-trade accord.

text.p: Bolivia and the Mercosur customs union on Friday put the final touches on a free-trade agreement that will double commerce between them to $1 billion in three years and expect to sign the accord in December, officials said.
The pact, which would take effect January 1, is likely to be signed December 17 at the Mercosur summit in the Brazilian city of Fortaleza, negotiators from Mercosur and the Andean country said.
"We are expecting exponential growth in our trade with Mercosur," as a result of the agreement, said Victor Rico, the Bolivian Foreign Ministry's secretary for foreign economic relations.

Thirteen months of talks ended "successfully" in Brasilia on Friday, the last day of a two-meeting of the Mercosur executive board, Jose Botafogo, Brazil's representative to four-nation customs union, said.
The officials said the agreement would be similar to one reached with Chile in July, which made Santiago an associate member of the union.
Annual trade between Bolivia and the Mercosur nations - Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay - now totals $500 million, including sales of Bolivian gas to Argentina.
Under the accord, that figure is expected to double in three years to $1 billion, roughly a third of Bolvia's total foreign trade.

Officials told reporters that accord would reduce tariffs to most products to zero over a 10-year period, with items on lists of "sensitive" products given an additional five to 10 years to eliminate tariffs.
"This is a trancendental moment in terms of regional integration," Rico said.
Apart from Chile and Bolivia, Venezuela and the five-nation Andean Part also are negotiating free trade pacts with Mercosur.
